text.p: Ten people were killed and dozens injured in an explosion in a Moscow cemetery on Sunday and one body was hurled 30 metres (yards) from the centre of the blast.

Reuter correspondent Artyom Danielyan said scores of officials had sealed off the blast site, in the Kotlyakovskoye cemetery in the south of the capital. He saw one mutilated body lying on a grave between two lines of police.
A police spokesman said 10 people had been killed and 30 had been injured.
The Interfax and Itar-Tass news agencies issued conflicting reports about the circumstances surrounding the blast.

Interfax, which said 70 people had been injured, said the blast took place about noon (0900 GMT) while a funeral ceremony was in progress. It said police said the explosion could have been a "settling of accounts" between organised crime groups.

Itar-Tass news agency said the explosion occurred during a ceremony commemorating Mikhail Likhodei, late head of the Afghan War Veterans' Foundation, who was blown up near his apartment block in 1994.
The head of another Afghan war veterans' group, which was involved in a dispute with Likhodei's, has been wounded in an apparent assassination attempt.

The incident was the latest in a series of explosions and gangland murders which have rocked Moscow during its tumultuous transition to a free market economy, which has been accompanied by a surge in the crime rate.
A week ago U.S. businessman Paul Tatum was killed in a hail of automatic gunfire at the entrance to a Moscow underground station.
Tatum's company Americom was locked in a bitter legal battle over ownership of the Radisson-Slavjanskaya hotel in central Moscow.
The gunman fled in a car after dropping a submachine gun at the Kievskaya metro station next to the Radisson-Slavjanskaya, where U.S. President Bill Clinton has stayed.
